questions.description: Questions to ask the user (1-4 questions)

question.description: The complete question to ask the user. Should be clear, specific, and end with a question mark. Example: "Which library should we use for date formatting?" If multiSelect is true, phrase it accordingly, e.g. "Which features do you want to enable?"

header.description: Very short label displayed as a chip/tag (max 12 chars). Examples: "Auth method", "Library", "Approach".

options.description: The available choices for this question. Must have 2-4 options. Each option should be a distinct, mutually exclusive choice (unless multiSelect is enabled). There should be no 'Other' option, that will be provided automatically.

label.description: The display text for this option that the user will see and select. Should be concise (1-5 words) and clearly describe the choice.

description.description: Explanation of what this option means or what will happen if chosen. Useful for providing context about trade-offs or implications.

preview.description: Optional preview content rendered when this option is focused. Use for mockups, code snippets, or visual comparisons that help users compare options. See the tool description for the expected content format.

multiSelect.description: Set to true to allow the user to select multiple options instead of just one. Use when choices are not mutually exclusive.

answers.description: User answers collected by the permission component

annotations.description: Optional per-question annotations from the user (e.g., notes on preview selections). Keyed by question text.

preview.description: The preview content of the selected option, if the question used previews.

notes.description: Free-text notes the user added to their selection.

metadata.description: Optional metadata for tracking and analytics purposes. Not displayed to user.

source.description: Optional identifier for the source of this question (e.g., "remember" for /remember command). Used for analytics tracking.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

# Branching policy — single `main` trunk + release-file prod promotion

This repo uses a **single long-lived branch (`main`) with a release-file prod promotion** (epic [#1480](https://github.com/iudexnc/inc-b2c-mvp/issues/1480), cutover [#1492](https://github.com/iudexnc/inc-b2c-mvp/issues/1492)). It replaces the short-lived dev/main split ([#1414](https://github.com/iudexnc/inc-b2c-mvp/issues/1414), 2026-07-02) — the promotion-as-code-merge model produced a bug per day (#1460, #1468, #1471, #1475) because it re-presented the whole batch diff as a PR; the release-file model promotes an **artifact pin**, not a code merge.

> **Diagram:** [branch model](diagrams/delivery/BRANCH-MODEL.md); deploy mechanics: [deployment-flow](diagrams/delivery/DEPLOYMENT-FLOW.md); promotion detail: [prod-daily-promotion](diagrams/delivery/PROD-DAILY-PROMOTION.md).

## The trunk

**`main` is the only long-lived branch and the repository default.** Every PR targets `main`; `Closes`/`Fixes`/`Resolves #N` auto-close on merge.

- **Every 6 hours on weekdays, every ~8 hours nights and weekends, from `main`** (split from a flat 2-hourly cadence by #8712 — Marina's decision, 2026-08-30; weekday slots thinned 8 → 3 by #12114 3a under epic #12109, 2026-09-17) → [`deploy-azure.yml`](../.github/workflows/deploy-azure.yml) (trigger `schedule:` — `0 6,12,18 * * 1-5` Mon-Fri 06/12/18:00 UTC, `0 0 * * 1-5` weekday midnight fill, `0 0,8,16 * * 0,6` the weekend 8h lattice) builds + deploys the **dev environment**, then on a green post-deploy smoke advances the **`dev-deployed`** git tag and moves the dev ACR **`:dev-green`** image alias onto the live dev digests. Every merge landing inside the window rides one deploy; a window with nothing new is a no-op, since change detection diffs against the per-target `dev-deployed-*` markers rather than a push range. It ran per-merge until #6102, then hourly until #6909, then flat 2-hourly until #8712 — the serial merge queue spaced merges ~14 min apart, so the push lane's supersession never coalesced anything and `main` produced 37 deploys for 40 merged PRs; the same arithmetic holds off-hours, where merge volume is lower still. A full off-hours pause was considered and rejected on #8712 (a Monday-morning or weekend dev would be many merges stale). Need dev updated sooner: `workflow_dispatch` on that workflow — and the marker half of it is `main`-only (#8261). A dispatch from any other ref still **deploys** dev, because a break-glass branch deploy is legitimate and the next scheduled run redeploys `main` over it; what it does not do is move any `dev-deployed*` marker, which is a `::notice::` per held marker and exit 0, never a failed run. A marker asserts what the environment runs and the daily prod promotion reads `dev-deployed` directly, so it must never name a commit that skipped the merge queue — on 2026-08-26 an unconstrained dispatch moved all four onto an intermediate commit of an unmerged branch. Enforced at the single `move_or_record()` chokepoint both marker paths call, by [`deploy-ref-permits-marker-move.sh`](../scripts/ci/deploy-ref-permits-marker-move.sh). **A green smoke does not always mean THIS run's commit is what advances the marker (#10263).** Two overlapping, uncancelled dev deploys (a manual dispatch racing the schedule) can both go green while only the later one's commit is actually serving; the older run's `post-deploy` smoke now recognises that shape (`deploy-provenance-supersession.sh`, comparing its own SHA against the served SHA's ancestry) and *accepts* rather than rolling back — a genuinely stale revision still fails as before. The **correspondence hold** in `advance-marker` then refuses to record that older run's own commit (`DEPLOY_SUPERSEDED`, a `::notice::` + exit 0, never a failed run): a marker asserts what the environment is running, and a superseded run did not place it. This is deliberately **not** a monotonicity guard — deploying an older commit on purpose still moves a marker backward, correctly — only a run whose own artifact was itself superseded before it could be recorded is held.
- **Prod never deploys from a push of ordinary code.** Prod is pinned by a tracked file and advances only when that file changes (below).

## The shared root checkout stays on `main`

Many agents run **in parallel from the same root checkout** and spawn worktrees off it, so that checkout is shared infrastructure, not a workspace. Two rules follow, and both are about what your local tree does to *other* agents:

- **Never `git checkout` / `git switch` the root checkout to a work branch.** Its branch is the base every other agent branches from; moving it silently puts all of them on the wrong base.
- **Never edit tracked files in it** — not even a throwaway experiment you mean to revert. `docker-test.sh` / `docker-eval.sh` build images **from the current tree**, so an uncommitted edit contaminates every other agent's run, and untangling it later needs a conflict-resolved transplant.

**Do branch work in a linked worktree** — [`.agents/skills/plan-build-isolated/SKILL.md`](../.agents/skills/plan-build-isolated/SKILL.md) Phase 0. The trigger is the **first edit of a tracked file**, for any reason, not the intent to ship.

**Recovery — root checkout found off `main`:** commit any uncommitted work **on the branch it is currently on** first (that work belongs to whoever left it there) — **under its real `type(scope): summary` subject, never `WIP` / `fixup!` / `squash!`**, because that commit is publishable the moment it is pushed and GitHub's squash merge takes its subject rather than the PR title, so anyone with merge rights can land a `WIP` subject on `main` permanently (#9556; canonical statement, with the two measured instances: [`git-commit-secure`](../.agents/skills/git-commit-secure/reference.md) § *Never `WIP` as a subject*) — a `PreToolUse` hook (`commit-subject-guard.sh`, same backstop-not-guarantee terms as the root-checkout hook below) now denies a `git commit -m` whose subject starts that way, in Claude Code sessions — then:

```bash
git checkout main && git pull
```

**The `root-checkout-guard.sh` hook is a backstop, not a guarantee.** [`.agents/settings.json`](../.agents/settings.json) wires a `PreToolUse` guard that denies a root-checkout `git checkout`/`switch` to anything but `main` (git-native root detection: `--git-dir` == `--git-common-dir`; `git checkout main` and pathspec restores stay allowed; `INC_ALLOW_ROOT_CHECKOUT=1` disables it). It **matches command text**, so an aliased `git`, a wrapper script, or an unusual quoting shape evades it — it raises the cost of the accidental case, which is the one that actually happens. **Cursor ignores Claude Code hooks entirely.** The prose invariant above is the source of truth; the hook is one tool's enforcement of it. Limits and the offline deny/allow matrix: [`scripts/automation/hooks/README.md`](../scripts/automation/hooks/README.md).

## The prod pin: `deploy/prod-release.json`

[`deploy/prod-release.json`](../deploy/README.md) on `main` records what production runs: `{schema, sha, api_digest, frontend_digest, promoted_at}` — the promoted commit plus the **exact dev-validated image digests** pinned at promotion time. Digests are pinned when the promotion PR opens, so a later dev deploy moving `:dev-green` never changes what an in-flight promotion ships.

**Rollback = a one-line revert PR** re-pinning the previous `sha`+digests. A rollback (non-descendant pin) always requires a security-reviewer approval (see gate below).

## Daily promotion (bump PR)

Once per day (04:40 UTC) [`promote-prod-release-daily.yml`](../.github/workflows/promote-prod-release-daily.yml) checks whether the last-green `dev-deployed` commit is ahead of the pin. If so it resolves the `:dev-green` digests, force-pushes a **one-commit `prod-release-bump` branch** updating only the release file, opens a **bot-authored bump PR** (the `iudexnc-prod-promotion` GitHub App; label `promotion`) whose body embeds a **reviewable batch listing** (every PR in `old-pin..new-pin`, 🛑 `security-high` / ⚠️ `security-medium` tiers surfaced first — see below), and enables **auto-merge (squash)**. Review is **mandatory on every promotion** (#2628) — there is no unattended auto-promote path; see the gate below. The PR's one-file diff still matches almost no path-triggered workflow, so promotion doesn't re-run the batch's checks (the #1475/#1477 storm class is gone by construction).

If the bump PR is still open the next night, the workflow **refreshes it in place** (new pin + regenerated batch listing) rather than closing and reopening — unless the pin and digests are unchanged, in which case it skips the force-push entirely so an in-force approval on the current head survives.

Merging the bump PR triggers [`deploy-prod-release.yml`](../.github/workflows/deploy-prod-release.yml): import the pinned digests cross-registry dev→prod ACR (no rebuild — byte-identical), repin the prod apps, smoke, and advance the **`prod-deployed`** tag to the pinned commit. Re-running after a transient failure is `workflow_dispatch` on that workflow (re-applies the current pin; it never chooses a different commit).

## Mandatory security review gate (#2628)

One gate, and it is GitHub's own. The bump PR **merges unreviewed by design** (the pin is a sha dev already proved green); the mandatory approval is the `production` GitHub Environment's required reviewers on the **deployment** that merge triggers, so [`deploy-prod-release.yml`](../.github/workflows/deploy-prod-release.yml)'s `deploy` job (and any break-glass production dispatch) stops at *Waiting for review* (#4906). The workflow-based predecessor — the `Require security review` required check posted by `promotion-security-gate.yml` — was archived in #4905.

**What that archived status check enforced, and where each part lives now.** None of it holds the *merge* any more — the environment gate above does — but the batch listing and one offline guard survived the archive:

- **Every promotion still needs an approval from [@iudexnc/security-reviewers](https://github.com/orgs/iudexnc/teams/security-reviewers)** — given on the *deployment*, as the `production` environment's required-reviewers rule (`can_admins_bypass: false`, #4906), never on the PR: the bump PR merges on its own and `deploy-prod-release.yml`'s `deploy` job waits. There is **no unattended auto-promote path** (#2628 supersedes the earlier rule that engaged the gate only when the batch carried `security-high`). The archived check resolved team membership at runtime through a short-lived `iudexnc-automation` app token minted with org members:read (#5117 rotation completed 2026-08-07, the legacy `SECURITY_REVIEWERS_TOKEN` PAT fallback removed); the environment rule needs no such plumbing — GitHub evaluates the team itself — and no workflow mints that token for membership any more. An approval is bound to one deployment attempt, so a refreshed pin (a new bump-PR merge, a new deploy run) needs a fresh approval.
- **The batch listing survived.** [`promote-prod-release-daily.yml`](../.github/workflows/promote-prod-release-daily.yml) still derives the batch from the **release-file diff** (`old-pin..new-pin`) and scans those commits' source-PR labels via [`collect-batch-pr-labels.sh`](../scripts/ci/collect-batch-pr-labels.sh) (fail-closed on an incomplete scan, #1439) to render the listing in the PR body — a `security-high` PR is surfaced at the top of it ("review with extra care") and gets `Potasya` requested as reviewer, but does not change *whether* review is required.
- **The release-file-shape invariants** the check enforced — a bump PR touching anything besides `deploy/prod-release.json` refused outright; a **digest-only** change (same commit, different image bytes) and a **non-descendant pin** (rollback / history rewrite) flagged in its verdict — went with it: nothing in `promote-prod-release-daily.yml`, `deploy-prod-release.yml` or `render-promotion-batch.sh` re-checks them. The reviewer of the deployment reads them off the one-file diff and the batch listing.
- The head-branch contract between the opener and `deploy-prod-release.yml` is still enforced offline by [`test-promotion-branch-consistency.sh`](../scripts/ci/test-promotion-branch-consistency.sh) (#1489: an incompletely-swept head rename once silently bypassed the gate; #4905 shrank its consumer list from five to one when the gate cluster was archived).

**A deployment waiting on the native gate is silent** — no red check, no PR signal, prod simply does not advance. Two mechanisms announce it, and both are guarded ([`validate-prod-approval-announce-wiring.sh`](../scripts/ci/validate-prod-approval-announce-wiring.sh), the `prod_approval` suite in [`selftests.yml`](../.github/workflows/selftests.yml)): [`notify-prod-approval.sh`](../scripts/ci/notify-prod-approval.sh) posts a pointer comment + Google Chat ping from a gate-free job on **both** prod entry paths — and on a **drift / break-glass entry, where there is no promotion PR and the ping is the only channel, a failed send reddens that job** rather than concluding `success` over an announcement nobody received (#7815); the job is gate-free and un-`needs:`-ed, so that red never blocks the deploy it announces — and [`prod-approval-nudge.yml`](../.github/workflows/prod-approval-nudge.yml) polls `waiting` runs as the state-based fail-safe — 15 min for an attempt nothing announced, then hourly escalation. The poll is repo-wide on purpose (#7319), but `waiting` is the state of a hold on **any** gated environment, so what gets announced is scoped per run to `production` ([`should-announce-prod-approval-run.sh`](../scripts/ci/should-announce-prod-approval-run.sh), #7433).

- **Two mechanisms announcing is not two mechanisms *notifying*** (#7797). Both POST to the same Google Chat webhook, and both did so with a `curl` that lacked `--fail` — which exits 0 on any response it receives, 404 included. A revoked or rotated `GCHAT_DEPLOY_WEBHOOK` therefore reported a delivered ping on both paths at once, and the nudge's bucket dedup then recorded the run as *already pinged* and stopped retrying. Observed on run `32695943118` (2026-08-24), which waited 2 h with both channels green and no message sent. Both calls now pass `--fail-with-body`, so a non-2xx is a loud `WARN` naming the webhook — still advisory, because this must never fail a deploy, but no longer silent. **A shared channel makes the redundancy correlated: the fail-safe and the thing it backs up fail together.**

- **Operator rule: re-run a waiting prod deploy with a FULL `gh run rerun <id>`, never `--failed`** (#5624). A partial re-run re-enters the approval gate but does **not** re-run the pointer job (`--failed` re-runs only failed jobs and their dependents), so the deployment waits unannounced until the nudge fires. A full re-run re-announces, because the pointer's dedup marker is per run **attempt**.

## Two-tier security label + reviewable batch listing (#2628)

The bump PR body embeds a **reviewable batch listing** — every PR in `old-pin..new-pin`, rendered by [`render-promotion-batch.sh`](../scripts/ci/render-promotion-batch.sh) from [`collect-batch-pr-labels.sh`](../scripts/ci/collect-batch-pr-labels.sh)'s `OUTPUT_MODE=prs` output — grouped 🛑 `security-high` first, ⚠️ `security-medium` next, everything else collapsed. Both labels stay **manual, author-applied** (the human author is the source of truth; the [`/gp`](../.agents/skills/git-protected-push/SKILL.md) skill assesses the surface and suggests, it doesn't decide); all five [PR templates](../.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/) carry a two-tier "Security level" prompt.

- **`security-medium`** (~10% of PRs — calibrate, don't overfire) — the old broad criteria: `infra/**`, `scripts/azure/**`, `.github/**` (workflows/CODEOWNERS/dependabot), auth/session/secret paths (`backend/src/azure/azureAuth.ts`, `backend/src/http/httpSecurity.ts`, `backend/src/server.ts`, `frontend/lib/auth/**`, `frontend/lib/server/**`), sensitive BFF surfaces (`frontend/app/api/auth|admin|internal|_lib|feedback/**`), rate limiting, the LLM untrusted-input boundary, `avbLoader`, `contracts/validation.ts`, any [CODEOWNERS](../.github/CODEOWNERS) path. Effect: visibility only — its own ⚠️ section in the batch listing.
- **`security-high`** (~1% of PRs — strict) — only: auth/secret **handling** changes (login wall, session issuance, secret storage/rotation); the promotion/deploy/review pipeline itself (deploy + promotion + security-gate workflows, `scripts/ci` gates, `deploy/prod-release.json` mechanics, branch-protection-relevant CI); privileged prod infra (`infra/**` changes that alter prod identities/permissions/network exposure). Rule of thumb: could this change weaken how code reaches prod, or who/what can access prod data? Effects: 🛑 top section of the batch listing, the promotion PR gets `Potasya` requested as reviewer, and it still blocks the manual break-glass prod deploy (below — unchanged, high-only).

The nightly promotion gate above no longer depends on either label — review is mandatory regardless. The labels now drive **visibility and routing**, not whether the gate engages.

## Manual break-glass prod deploy stays conditional on `security-high`

The manual [`deploy-azure.yml`](../.github/workflows/deploy-azure.yml) `workflow_dispatch environment=production` deploy remains for emergencies. Unlike the now-mandatory nightly promotion gate above, this path is **unchanged by #2628**: its **`production-security-gate`** job (#1393) refuses the dispatch when the batch it would ship (`prod-deployed`..`HEAD`) contains a `security-high` PR — using the same [`collect-batch-pr-labels.sh`](../scripts/ci/collect-batch-pr-labels.sh) batch-label source as the bump PR's gate — pointing the operator at the gated bump PR instead (where a security reviewer can approve). A non-security batch deploys unattended. The block/allow decision is made by the regression-tested [`gate-manual-prod-deploy.sh`](../scripts/ci/gate-manual-prod-deploy.sh) (not inline YAML), which **fails closed** on the collector's `__label-collection-incomplete__` sentinel and on any hard collector error — an incomplete label scan could have dropped a real `security-high`, so it is refused exactly like a security batch, mirroring the archived sibling `require-security-review.sh` gate (#1439/#1455). # Branching policy — single `main` trunk + release-file prod promotion

This repo uses a **single long-lived branch (`main`) with a release-file prod promotion** (epic [#1480](https://github.com/iudexnc/inc-b2c-mvp/issues/1480), cutover [#1492](https://github.com/iudexnc/inc-b2c-mvp/issues/1492)). It replaces the short-lived dev/main split ([#1414](https://github.com/iudexnc/inc-b2c-mvp/issues/1414), 2026-07-02) — the promotion-as-code-merge model produced a bug per day (#1460, #1468, #1471, #1475) because it re-presented the whole batch diff as a PR; the release-file model promotes an **artifact pin**, not a code merge.

> **Diagram:** [branch model](diagrams/delivery/BRANCH-MODEL.md); deploy mechanics: [deployment-flow](diagrams/delivery/DEPLOYMENT-FLOW.md); promotion detail: [prod-daily-promotion](diagrams/delivery/PROD-DAILY-PROMOTION.md).

## The trunk

**`main` is the only long-lived branch and the repository default.** Every PR targets `main`; `Closes`/`Fixes`/`Resolves #N` auto-close on merge.

- **Every 6 hours on weekdays, every ~8 hours nights and weekends, from `main`** (split from a flat 2-hourly cadence by #8712 — Marina's decision, 2026-08-30; weekday slots thinned 8 → 3 by #12114 3a under epic #12109, 2026-09-17) → [`deploy-azure.yml`](../.github/workflows/deploy-azure.yml) (trigger `schedule:` — `0 6,12,18 * * 1-5` Mon-Fri 06/12/18:00 UTC, `0 0 * * 1-5` weekday midnight fill, `0 0,8,16 * * 0,6` the weekend 8h lattice) builds + deploys the **dev environment**, then on a green post-deploy smoke advances the **`dev-deployed`** git tag and moves the dev ACR **`:dev-green`** image alias onto the live dev digests. Every merge landing inside the window rides one deploy; a window with nothing new is a no-op, since change detection diffs against the per-target `dev-deployed-*` markers rather than a push range. It ran per-merge until #6102, then hourly until #6909, then flat 2-hourly until #8712 — the serial merge queue spaced merges ~14 min apart, so the push lane's supersession never coalesced anything and `main` produced 37 deploys for 40 merged PRs; the same arithmetic holds off-hours, where merge volume is lower still. A full off-hours pause was considered and rejected on #8712 (a Monday-morning or weekend dev would be many merges stale). Need dev updated sooner: `workflow_dispatch` on that workflow — and the marker half of it is `main`-only (#8261). A dispatch from any other ref still **deploys** dev, because a break-glass branch deploy is legitimate and the next scheduled run redeploys `main` over it; what it does not do is move any `dev-deployed*` marker, which is a `::notice::` per held marker and exit 0, never a failed run. A marker asserts what the environment runs and the daily prod promotion reads `dev-deployed` directly, so it must never name a commit that skipped the merge queue — on 2026-08-26 an unconstrained dispatch moved all four onto an intermediate commit of an unmerged branch. Enforced at the single `move_or_record()` chokepoint both marker paths call, by [`deploy-ref-permits-marker-move.sh`](../scripts/ci/deploy-ref-permits-marker-move.sh). **A green smoke does not always mean THIS run's commit is what advances the marker (#10263).** Two overlapping, uncancelled dev deploys (a manual dispatch racing the schedule) can both go green while only the later one's commit is actually serving; the older run's `post-deploy` smoke now recognises that shape (`deploy-provenance-supersession.sh`, comparing its own SHA against the served SHA's ancestry) and *accepts* rather than rolling back — a genuinely stale revision still fails as before. The **correspondence hold** in `advance-marker` then refuses to record that older run's own commit (`DEPLOY_SUPERSEDED`, a `::notice::` + exit 0, never a failed run): a marker asserts what the environment is running, and a superseded run did not place it. This is deliberately **not** a monotonicity guard — deploying an older commit on purpose still moves a marker backward, correctly — only a run whose own artifact was itself superseded before it could be recorded is held.
- **Prod never deploys from a push of ordinary code.** Prod is pinned by a tracked file and advances only when that file changes (below).

## The shared root checkout stays on `main`

Many agents run **in parallel from the same root checkout** and spawn worktrees off it, so that checkout is shared infrastructure, not a workspace. Two rules follow, and both are about what your local tree does to *other* agents:

- **Never `git checkout` / `git switch` the root checkout to a work branch.** Its branch is the base every other agent branches from; moving it silently puts all of them on the wrong base.
- **Never edit tracked files in it** — not even a throwaway experiment you mean to revert. `docker-test.sh` / `docker-eval.sh` build images **from the current tree**, so an uncommitted edit contaminates every other agent's run, and untangling it later needs a conflict-resolved transplant.

**Do branch work in a linked worktree** — [`.agents/skills/plan-build-isolated/SKILL.md`](../.agents/skills/plan-build-isolated/SKILL.md) Phase 0. The trigger is the **first edit of a tracked file**, for any reason, not the intent to ship.

**Recovery — root checkout found off `main`:** commit any uncommitted work **on the branch it is currently on** first (that work belongs to whoever left it there) — **under its real `type(scope): summary` subject, never `WIP` / `fixup!` / `squash!`**, because that commit is publishable the moment it is pushed and GitHub's squash merge takes its subject rather than the PR title, so anyone with merge rights can land a `WIP` subject on `main` permanently (#9556; canonical statement, with the two measured instances: [`git-commit-secure`](../.agents/skills/git-commit-secure/reference.md) § *Never `WIP` as a subject*) — a `PreToolUse` hook (`commit-subject-guard.sh`, same backstop-not-guarantee terms as the root-checkout hook below) now denies a `git commit -m` whose subject starts that way, in Claude Code sessions — then:

```bash
git checkout main && git pull
```

**The `root-checkout-guard.sh` hook is a backstop, not a guarantee.** [`.agents/settings.json`](../.agents/settings.json) wires a `PreToolUse` guard that denies a root-checkout `git checkout`/`switch` to anything but `main` (git-native root detection: `--git-dir` == `--git-common-dir`; `git checkout main` and pathspec restores stay allowed; `INC_ALLOW_ROOT_CHECKOUT=1` disables it). It **matches command text**, so an aliased `git`, a wrapper script, or an unusual quoting shape evades it — it raises the cost of the accidental case, which is the one that actually happens. **Cursor ignores Claude Code hooks entirely.** The prose invariant above is the source of truth; the hook is one tool's enforcement of it. Limits and the offline deny/allow matrix: [`scripts/automation/hooks/README.md`](../scripts/automation/hooks/README.md).

## The prod pin: `deploy/prod-release.json`

[`deploy/prod-release.json`](../deploy/README.md) on `main` records what production runs: `{schema, sha, api_digest, frontend_digest, promoted_at}` — the promoted commit plus the **exact dev-validated image digests** pinned at promotion time. Digests are pinned when the promotion PR opens, so a later dev deploy moving `:dev-green` never changes what an in-flight promotion ships.

**Rollback = a one-line revert PR** re-pinning the previous `sha`+digests. A rollback (non-descendant pin) always requires a security-reviewer approval (see gate below).

## Daily promotion (bump PR)

Once per day (04:40 UTC) [`promote-prod-release-daily.yml`](../.github/workflows/promote-prod-release-daily.yml) checks whether the last-green `dev-deployed` commit is ahead of the pin. If so it resolves the `:dev-green` digests, force-pushes a **one-commit `prod-release-bump` branch** updating only the release file, opens a **bot-authored bump PR** (the `iudexnc-prod-promotion` GitHub App; label `promotion`) whose body embeds a **reviewable batch listing** (every PR in `old-pin..new-pin`, 🛑 `security-high` / ⚠️ `security-medium` tiers surfaced first — see below), and enables **auto-merge (squash)**. Review is **mandatory on every promotion** (#2628) — there is no unattended auto-promote path; see the gate below. The PR's one-file diff still matches almost no path-triggered workflow, so promotion doesn't re-run the batch's checks (the #1475/#1477 storm class is gone by construction).

If the bump PR is still open the next night, the workflow **refreshes it in place** (new pin + regenerated batch listing) rather than closing and reopening — unless the pin and digests are unchanged, in which case it skips the force-push entirely so an in-force approval on the current head survives.

Merging the bump PR triggers [`deploy-prod-release.yml`](../.github/workflows/deploy-prod-release.yml): import the pinned digests cross-registry dev→prod ACR (no rebuild — byte-identical), repin the prod apps, smoke, and advance the **`prod-deployed`** tag to the pinned commit. Re-running after a transient failure is `workflow_dispatch` on that workflow (re-applies the current pin; it never chooses a different commit).

One gate, and it is GitHub's own. The bump PR **merges unreviewed by design** (the pin is a sha dev already proved green); the mandatory approval is the `production` GitHub Environment's required reviewers on the **deployment** that merge triggers, so [`deploy-prod-release.yml`](../.github/workflows/deploy-prod-release.yml)'s `deploy` job (and any break-glass production dispatch) stops at *Waiting for review* (#4906). The workflow-based predecessor — the `Require security review` required check posted by `promotion-security-gate.yml` — was archived in #4905.

- **Every promotion still needs an approval from [@iudexnc/security-reviewers](https://github.com/orgs/iudexnc/teams/security-reviewers)** — given on the *deployment*, as the `production` environment's required-reviewers rule (`can_admins_bypass: false`, #4906), never on the PR: the bump PR merges on its own and `deploy-prod-release.yml`'s `deploy` job waits. There is **no unattended auto-promote path** (#2628 supersedes the earlier rule that engaged the gate only when the batch carried `security-high`). The archived check resolved team membership at runtime through a short-lived `iudexnc-automation` app token minted with org members:read (#5117 rotation completed 2026-08-07, the legacy `SECURITY_REVIEWERS_TOKEN` PAT fallback removed); the environment rule needs no such plumbing — GitHub evaluates the team itself — and no workflow mints that token for membership any more. An approval is bound to one deployment attempt, so a refreshed pin (a new bump-PR merge, a new deploy run) needs a fresh approval.

# Isolated plan → build (`inc-b2c-mvp`)

Plan and implement **never directly on `main`**, **never on a dirty unrelated checkout**, and **never by switching the shared root checkout's branch** (it stays on `main` — parallel agents share it). Use a dedicated branch from **`origin/main`** (**`feat/`**, **`fix/`**, **`chore/`**, or **`refactor/`**), then build, verify, and ask whether to publish.

**Complements** [`refactor-plan-implement`](../refactor-plan-implement/SKILL.md) (`/refactor-loop`) — refactor-audit focused; does **not** isolate branches upfront.

## When to activate (agents)

| Trigger | Scope |
|---------|--------|
| User clicks **Build** or **Build in New Agent** on an approved Plan mode plan | Phase 0 **first** (plan already done → skip Phase 1) |
| User says **`/plan-build`**, **plan and build**, **plan then build**, **plan + build** | Phase 0 → Phase 1 → … |
| User says **build**, **implement**, **execute** the plan (same thread or new agent spawned from plan UI) | Phase 0 **first** unless already isolated (below) |
| **First edit of a tracked file in the shared root checkout — for ANY reason** (experiment, spike, eval arm, one-line probe, "I'll revert it") | Phase 0 **first**; the trigger is the edit, not the intent to ship |

3. Derive **`<branch>`** = **`<prefix>/<short-slug>`** (same prefixes as [`git-protected-push`](../git-protected-push/SKILL.md)):
   - **`feat/`** — default for new user-facing work
   - **`fix/`** — bugfixes
   - **`refactor/`** — structural changes without new product behavior
   - **`chore/`** — tooling, deps, skills/rules, config
   - Infer prefix from plan title, user words (fix/bug/refactor/chore), or task type
   - User named a prefix → use it if in the list above
   - Unique on **`origin`** — append `-2`, `-3`, … if needed
4. Choose isolation mode (use **`<branch>`** — do **not** hardcode **`feat/`**):

| Condition | Action |
|-----------|--------|
| CWD already inside **any** worktree (**`~/.cursor/worktrees/`**, **`.agents/worktrees/*`**, **`../inc-b2c-mvp-*`**; **`--git-dir`** ≠ **`--git-common-dir`**, step 2) | **`git checkout -b <branch> origin/main`** — never nest a second worktree |
| Shared root checkout — **dirty or clean** (it stays on `main`; parallel agents and new worktrees depend on it) | Capture **`ROOT_WORKTREE_PATH="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"`**, then **`git worktree add ../inc-b2c-mvp-<slug> -b <branch> origin/main`** → **`cd`** there → step 5 |

**Claude Code shortcut for the second row:** **`EnterWorktree`** with **`name`** = **`<branch>`** does all of step 4 and half of step 5 — the `WorktreeCreate` hook creates the worktree at **`../inc-b2c-mvp-wt/<slug>`** (under **`$INC_WORKTREE_BASE_DIR`** when exported — `/mnt/worktrees` on the shared VM) on that exact branch off **`origin/main`** and carries **`.env.local`** in, leaving only the install in step 5. **Never `npm ci` in a worktree** — npm follows its `node_modules` symlinks into the main checkout and destroys *main's* install (#8200); `worktree-install-deps.sh` purges them first and installs offline from the npm cache. It was unusable here until the hook landed (the committed **`.claude`** symlink makes Claude Code refuse managed worktrees); `git worktree add` stays the path for Cursor and for any non-conventional base ref.

**Shell shapes the isolation check refuses, once inside.** After `EnterWorktree` or a manual worktree, Claude Code's own guard ("This session is isolated in the worktree … too complex to verify") refuses some Bash calls outright — 358/858 failed Bash calls (42%) in a 60-transcript sample, 2026-09-04..23, ~10 per worktree session; 329/357 succeeded unchanged on the very next call. Refused shapes: a compound command naming `git` (often innocently — a `.github/` path, a GitHub URL, or an unrelated `git` substring); heredocs; pipes; redirects into the scratchpad; `bash` inside a construct; Python text naming `git`; `cd <worktree>` inside a compound command. Safe alternatives: run from the worktree root without `cd`; one `git` command per Bash call; keep `.github/` paths and GitHub URLs out of compound commands; write a multi-line script to a file and run it instead of a heredoc. Harness-version dependent — re-check before trusting this if it stops matching. More detail and measured pairs: [reference.md § *Commands the isolation guard refuses*](reference.md#commands-the-isolation-guard-refuses-8661).

5. **Worktree setup** (only when a new worktree was created in step 4):

```bash
cd ../inc-b2c-mvp-<slug>
./scripts/local/worktree-install-deps.sh
test -f "$ROOT_WORKTREE_PATH/.env.local" && cp "$ROOT_WORKTREE_PATH/.env.local" .env.local || true
```

Matches [`.cursor/worktrees.json`](../../../.cursor/worktrees.json) **`setup-worktree-unix`** — keep in sync.
A worktree holding `.hygiene-deps-reclaimed` (the hygiene sweep reclaimed its idle `node_modules`) needs the same install.
So does a worktree after a `git merge origin/main` (or rebase) that changes `package-lock.json`: git does not update `node_modules`, and the gates refuse until it matches (#8204). One that changes only `shared/src` needs just `npm run build -w shared` in your own worktree: the legs that read `shared/dist` refuse until it matches (#13829, #13847).

6. **Report** branch name and path before editing files.
7. **Tracking issue (offer, don't block).** GitHub is the single source of truth for execution — new work should be tracked by an issue so the backlog is a complete record. If the task is **not already tied to an issue** (the user named none and the plan carries no `Fixes`/`Closes`/`Refs #N`) **and** it is non-trivial new work, **check for competitors first** (`gh pr list --search <topic>` + `git ls-remote origin 'fix/*'`), then **offer** to open one:

   > This isn't linked to an issue — want me to open a tracking issue first (`scripts/automation/queue/create-claimed-issue.sh`, `bug` for a deterministic defect — unit-test red, no live model call — else `backlog`)? I can proceed either way.

   On **yes**, run `scripts/automation/queue/create-claimed-issue.sh` — it creates the issue **and** claims it in the same step (`claim-issue.sh` under the hood), not a bare `gh issue create`, so the automation queue can't legitimately pick up the same issue while you're already working it (the gap behind #3084→#3099/#3114, #3094→#3118/#3117, #3143→#3162). Claiming is right **here** only because you start building immediately; any *other* issue this task spawns — a follow-up, a sibling you'll take later, a batch of epic children — is filed `--for-queue` (unclaimed) and claimed later via `claim-issue.sh <N>` when it is actually started ([issue-label-lifecycle](../../rules/issue-label-lifecycle.mdc)). Thread its number into the eventual PR body (**`Fixes #N`** for a defect, **`Closes #N`** otherwise, **`Refs #N`** if partial). If the claim comes back contested, stop and report — someone else already owns that issue. On **no / skip**, proceed — the post-merge net in [`pr-bot-review-queue.yml`](../../../.github/workflows/pr-bot-review-queue.yml)'s janitor auto-creates a tracking issue if it merges unlinked, on that file's cron (#11606). Never gate editing on the answer.

Phase 0 is the **single owner** of the worktree procedure — [`git-commit-secure`](../git-commit-secure/SKILL.md) § *Isolate in a worktree when the tree is busy* points here for the commands and adds only its own trigger conditions. Do not restate the recipe elsewhere; a recipe that omits the **`origin/main`** base is the stale-base duplicate-commit bug.

# Claude Code hooks

Committed hooks wired from [`.agents/settings.json`](../../../.agents/settings.json) (which
`.claude/settings.json` symlinks to). They exist so that rules which are **deterministic and
always true** stop being carried as always-on prose.

**Why hooks instead of prose** (epic #4714, issue #4719): an "always do X" / "never do X" rule in
`AGENTS.md` or an always-on `.agents/rules/*.mdc` is charged to *every* turn and is still only a
request the model may or may not honour. The same rule as a hook costs **zero context** and is a
**guarantee**. Prose is for judgment; hooks are for invariants.

| Hook | Event | Fires when | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`claim-first-reminder.sh`](claim-first-reminder.sh) | `UserPromptSubmit` | the prompt mentions `#NNN` / an issues URL / "issue NNN" | injects the claim-first reminder (non-blocking) |

| [`masked-exit-status-guard.sh`](masked-exit-status-guard.sh) | `PreToolUse` (Bash) | a command **runs** (in command position, not merely names) a verdict-bearing script — anything under `scripts/local/`, a `scripts/lib/test-*.sh` suite, `verify-changes`/`security-scan`/`security-gate`/`verify-local`/`docker-test*`, or an `npm … test*` lane — and masks its status: a `$?` read that captures nothing, `\|\| true`/`\|\| :`, or a pipeline in which it is not the last stage | **deny** — the sequence would exit 0 on a failed gate |
| [`pr-arm-guard.sh`](pr-arm-guard.sh) | `PreToolUse` (Bash) | a hand-typed `gh pr ready` or `gh pr merge` at statement position (`--undo`, `--disable-auto` and `--help` excepted; a quoted, heredoc or comment mention is not an invocation) | **deny** — the ready flip and the arm are `gp-publish.sh`'s, on a green publish receipt (#12639); a PR that is not this head is armed through `agent-action.sh --action pr-arm-automerge`, which refuses a draft |
| [`gh-claim-label-guard.sh`](gh-claim-label-guard.sh) | `PreToolUse` (Bash, GitHub MCP) | a **claim-transport** label (`issue-taken`, `bot-review-taken`, `bot-review-pending`) or `needs-human` is added/removed by hand | **deny** — the lock ref and the label ride separate transports; use the claim scripts / `park-for-human.sh` |
| [`commit-subject-guard.sh`](commit-subject-guard.sh) | `PreToolUse` (Bash) | `git commit` (or `-m`/`--message` literal, single/double-quoted, or the `-m "$(cat <<EOF … EOF)"` trailer shape) has a subject starting `WIP`, `fixup!` or `squash!` | **deny** — GitHub's squash merge carries the commit subject onto `main` verbatim (#9556) |
| [`draft-first-publish-guard.sh`](draft-first-publish-guard.sh) | `PreToolUse` (Bash) | `gh pr create` carries no `--draft` | **deny** — every PR opens as a draft (#12113); on a draft the three required contexts red in seconds instead of verifying a tree nobody has finished. Use `/gp`, or add `--draft` |
| [`shell-job-guard.sh`](shell-job-guard.sh) | `PreToolUse` (Bash, Monitor) | `pgrep -f`/`pkill -f` inside an `until`/`while` loop, a broad `pkill -f`/`kill $(pgrep -f …)`/`pgrep -f … \| xargs kill`/`killall`, or a **background** `until`/`while`/`tail -f` wait with no deadline and no liveness test; **advises** on a background launch, a one-shot `pgrep -f`, a long or looped `sleep` | **deny** the self-match, pattern-kill and unbounded-background-wait shapes; otherwise non-blocking `additionalContext` (each class once per session) pointing to the delisted skill [`shell-jobs`](../../../.agents/skills/shell-jobs/SKILL.md). On Monitor (bounded by its own `timeout_ms`) only the denies and the `pgrep -f` advice apply |
| [`red-test-lock-guard.sh`](red-test-lock-guard.sh) | `PreToolUse` (Edit, Write, MultiEdit) | the edited path is named by a `Red-Test: <path>` trailer on a commit of this branch (since merge-base with `origin/main`) with no later `Red-Test-Unlock: <path>` | **deny** — the reproducing test's red is committed (bugfix Phase 1), so the fix goes in production code, never the test (#12101). Structured state only: git's own trailer parser, exact path compare, replayed in commit order |
| [`read-telemetry.sh`](read-telemetry.sh) | `PostToolUse` (Read/Skill) | an **instruction** file is read (`AGENTS.md`, `.agents/rules/*`, `.agents/skills/*/*.md`, `.agents/commands/*.md`) | **records** `{ts, path}` to a gitignored log — not a guard |
| [`push-receipt-probe.sh`](push-receipt-probe.sh) | `PreToolUse` (Bash) | `git push` or `gp-publish.sh` at statement position (not `--dry-run`/`--delete`) | **records** one `push-probe` row in the gate ledger: branch, HEAD, clean, and whether a green `verify-changes.sh` receipt covers the tree (`valid`/`stale`/`none`) — the #12326 measurement, not a guard |
| [`run-id-stamp.sh`](run-id-stamp.sh) | `UserPromptSubmit` | every prompt | **records** this session's run id to `.agents/telemetry/run-id` (gitignored), so a later shell call can recover it — not a guard |
| [`run-trace-emit.sh`](run-trace-emit.sh) | `Stop`, `SubagentStop` | end of every turn (cloud: end of run); a subagent finishing | **emits** one redacted `run-trace/v0` commit on a ref for the harvester, the latest turn winning; a worktree subagent gets its own ref at its worktree's HEAD (#12829) — not a guard, and the only hook here that **touches the network** |

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# root-checkout-guard.sh: Claude Code `PreToolUse` guard for Bash.
#
# Enforces "the root checkout stays on `main`" (AGENTS.md § Branching). Many
# agents run in parallel from the shared root checkout and spawn worktrees off
# it, so switching its branch silently puts every other agent on the wrong base.
#
# Denies `git checkout` / `git switch` to anything other than `main` WHEN the
# command would run in the ROOT checkout. A linked worktree is unaffected, that
# is where branch work belongs.
#
# BACKSTOP, NOT A REPLACEMENT: like the push guard, this matches command text, so
# regex evasion is possible (an aliased git, a script wrapper, a here-doc). It
# raises the cost of the accidental case (which is the one that actually happens),
# it does not make the rule unbypassable. The prose invariant remains the
# source of truth for tools that ignore hooks (Cursor). Epic #4714, issue #4719.
#
# Root-checkout detection is the git-native one, not a path comparison:
#   `git rev-parse --git-dir` == `--git-common-dir`  ->  root checkout
#   in a linked worktree, --git-dir is <common>/worktrees/<name>  ->  they differ
#
# ESCAPE HATCHES:
#   * `git checkout main` / `git switch main` is always allowed: it IS the
#     documented remediation for a root checkout found off main.
#   * pathspec restores (`git checkout -- <path>`, `git checkout <existing-file>`)
#     are allowed; they do not move HEAD.
#   * export INC_ALLOW_ROOT_CHECKOUT=1 to disable the guard entirely.
#
# Wired from `.agents/settings.json` (= `.claude/settings.json`) on Bash.
# Offline deny/allow matrix: test-root-checkout-guard.sh (run by queue-selftest.yml).
#
# `set -f`: this guard word-splits untrusted command text (the target-ref loop
# below). Without it, a command containing `*` would glob against the CWD and
# the guard would inspect filenames instead of the argument it was given.
set -euo pipefail
set -f

[ "${INC_ALLOW_ROOT_CHECKOUT:-}" = "1" ] && exit 0

input=$(cat)
cmd=$(printf '%s' "$input" | jq -r '.tool_input.command // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
[ -z "$cmd" ] && exit 0

# Cheap pre-filter: no checkout/switch token at all -> nothing to do.
# Here-string, never `printf … |` (#7736): this guard FAILS OPEN on `|| exit 0`, so a writer
# SIGPIPEd by the matcher's early exit would hand pipefail a 141 and ALLOW the very checkout
# it just matched. `<<<` is safe for a different reason than "it is a file": bash writes the
# WHOLE payload before exec'ing the reader — into the pipe buffer when it fits, a temp file when
# it does not — so there is never a partial write left to be SIGPIPEd.
grep -Eq '(^|[^[:alnum:]_])(checkout|switch)([^[:alnum:]_]|$)' <<<"$cmd" || exit 0

# --- sanitise -------------------------------------------------------------
# Same treatment as inc-b2c-mvp-push-guard.sh: drop heredoc bodies and quoted
# spans, so a command whose *payload text* merely mentions a checkout (a commit
# message, a PR body, this file's own diff) cannot false-positive. Deliberately
# duplicated rather than shared: the push guard is COPIED standalone into
# ~/.claude/hooks/ by install-guard.sh, so it cannot source a library, and a
# guard that silently loses its sanitiser is worse than one that repeats it.
# Keep the two in sync when either changes.
#
# The quote stripping is a STATE MACHINE that persists across newlines, not a
# per-line regex (issue #5917). The line-oriented sed pair it replaces let a quoted
# span spanning several lines leave its closing quote dangling at the start of the
# final line; that dangling quote paired with the NEXT legitimate quote on the line
# and the regex deleted everything between them — removing the real invocation from
# `$scan` entirely. The heredoc half of this same block was already multi-line-aware;
# the quote half was not, and the mismatch is what flipped parity. Unterminated
# spans are re-emitted at END so a stray quote cannot silently swallow the rest of
# the command (fail-closed: the residual risk is a false DENY on a malformed
# command, the safe direction for a guard).
scan=$(printf '%s' "$cmd" | awk '
  function strip_quotes(line,   out, i, c, n) {
    out = ""; n = length(line)
    for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
      c = substr(line, i, 1)
      if (qs == "") {
        # Outside a span, a backslash escapes the next character, so `\"` opens
        # nothing. Both characters are KEPT: `\gh` must survive intact for the
        # CMD_PREFIX matcher below.
        if (c == "\\") { out = out c; if (i < n) { i++; out = out substr(line, i, 1) } }
        else if (c == SQ || c == DQ) { qs = c; pending = c }
        else out = out c
      } else if (qs == DQ && c == "\\") {
        # Inside "..." a backslash escapes the next char; neither closes the span.
        pending = pending c
        if (i < n) { i++; pending = pending substr(line, i, 1) }
      } else if (c == qs) {
        qs = ""; pending = ""
      } else {
        pending = pending c
      }
    }
    # A span still open here continues onto the next line — record the newline so a
    # re-emitted unterminated span keeps its shape.
    if (qs != "") pending = pending "\n"
    return out
  }
  BEGIN { inhere = 0; q = "[\047\042]?"; SQ = "\047"; DQ = "\042"; qs = ""; pending = "" }
  {
    if (inhere == 1) { t = $0; sub(/^[ \t]+/, "", t); if (t == delim) inhere = 0; next }
    re = "<<-?[ \t]*" q "[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*" q
    if (match($0, re)) {
      seg = substr($0, RSTART, RLENGTH); sub(/^<<-?[ \t]*/, "", seg); gsub(/[\047\042]/, "", seg)
      delim = seg; inhere = 1
    }
    print strip_quotes($0)
  }
  END { if (qs != "") print pending }')

# Statement-boundary matcher, skipping a legal leading `NAME=VALUE ` run
# (the #1349 evasion the push guard closed).
ASSIGN_RUN='([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*=[^[:space:]]*[[:space:]]+)*'
# Here-string: the second fail-open `|| exit 0` (#7736, see the pre-filter above).
grep -Eq "(^|[;&|(])[[:space:]]*${ASSIGN_RUN}git([^[:alnum:]_]|$)" <<<"$scan" || exit 0

# Isolate the `git … checkout|switch …` statement itself.
# `(checkout|switch)($|[^&|;[:alnum:]_][^&|;]*)` is the portable spelling of the old
# `(checkout|switch)\b[^&|;]*` (#5582): `\b` is zero-width, so the boundary has to become a
# CONSUMED non-word char, and it must exclude the statement separators the tail already
# stops at, or `git checkout;` would capture the `;` and read as a targeted checkout.
# TWO distinct failure modes are guarded on this one line; both fixes are load-bearing and
# neither subsumes the other.
#
# `|| true` (#5731): under `set -e` + `pipefail` the grep exits 1 when the command carries some
# OTHER git subcommand, and the assignment would abort the hook right here — before the
# `[ -z "$seg" ]` fallback below that exists precisely for that case.
#
# `sed -n '1p'`, never `head -1` (#5737): `head` stops reading after line 1 while the external
# grep is still writing, so the grep takes SIGPIPE and exits 141. `|| true` would swallow that
# too — but only after the fact: the real cost is that a 141 is indistinguishable from "no
# match", so a command that DOES contain a checkout silently reads as `seg=""` and the guard
# exits 0, which Claude Code reads as ALLOW. `sed` has no `q` and reads to EOF, so the writer
# is never signalled and rc 1 means what it says.
seg=$(printf '%s' "$scan" | grep -Eo 'git[[:space:]]+(-C[[:space:]]+[^[:space:]]+[[:space:]]+)?(-[^[:space:]]+[[:space:]]+)*(checkout|switch)($|[^&|;[:alnum:]_][^&|;]*)' | sed -n '1p' || true)
[ -z "$seg" ] && exit 0

# --- which directory(ies) would this run in? --------------------------------
# Fail-closed union (issue #5668 sibling sweep, mirroring the fix applied to
# inc-b2c-mvp-push-guard.sh in the same PR). Pre-fix, a single best-guess `dir`
# (cwd, overridden by the first `cd`/`-C` found regardless of whether it
# actually governs THIS checkout/switch statement) let a trailing decoy `cd`
# after the real checkout reroute `dir` to a bogus path: `git checkout
# feat/evil && cd /tmp` rerouted to /tmp, the repo-gate exited 0 on it, and the
# switch went unchecked. Fix: union of every plausible candidate; a decoy can
# only ADD scrutiny, never remove it.
base_dir=$(printf '%s' "$input" | jq -r '.cwd // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
[ -z "$base_dir" ] && base_dir="${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-$PWD}"

if [ -z "$base_dir" ]; then
  jq -n --arg r "Blocked: could not determine the target directory for this checkout/switch, so it cannot be confirmed safe. Do branch work in a worktree (git worktree add -b <branch> ../wt-<slug> origin/main)." \
    '{hookSpecificOutput:{hookEventName:"PreToolUse",permissionDecision:"deny",permissionDecisionReason:$r}}'
  exit 0
fi

dirs="$base_dir"

# `cd <path>`: only one occurring BEFORE the isolated checkout/switch
# statement. A `cd` typed AFTER it (the decoy above) does not change where the
# switch ran, so it is not added as a candidate; base_dir alone still catches it.
seg_at=$(printf '%s' "$scan" \
  | grep -boE 'git[[:space:]]+(-C[[:space:]]+[^[:space:]]+[[:space:]]+)?(-[^[:space:]]+[[:space:]]+)*(checkout|switch)($|[^&|;[:alnum:]_][^&|;]*)' \
  | sed -n '1p' | cut -d: -f1 || true)
cd_scope="$scan"
# N is a 0-indexed byte OFFSET (from grep -b), so it can be 0 — and here 0 is
# the COMMON case, not a corner: it means the command starts with `git
# checkout …`. A 0 is not safe to hand to a byte-count tool: `cut -c1-0` is an
# invalid decreasing range, and BSD / macOS `head -c 0` is a hard error
# ("illegal byte count") where GNU head quietly yields "". Under `set -euo
# pipefail` that error KILLED this guard, it emitted nothing, and Claude Code
# reads no-output as ALLOW — so on macOS every plain `git checkout <branch>` in
# the root checkout sailed through (11 of this guard's own matrix rows fail
# there, all green on ubuntu-latest CI). Take the empty prefix directly rather
# than asking head for zero bytes (issue #5668; the macos-latest job added to
# queue-selftest.yml in the same change is what keeps CI honest about it).
if [ -n "$seg_at" ]; then
  if [ "$seg_at" -gt 0 ]; then
    cd_scope=$(head -c "$seg_at" <<<"$scan")
  else
    cd_scope=""
  fi
fi
cd_targets=$(printf '%s' "$cd_scope" | grep -Eo '(^|[;&|(])[[:space:]]*cd[[:space:]]+[^[:space:];&|]+' \
  | sed -E 's/^[^c]*cd[[:space:]]+//' || true)

# issue #7033: base_dir (the session cwd) is a PLAUSIBLE candidate only when
# the checkout could still actually run there. When the LAST `cd` before the
# isolated checkout/switch statement is joined to it by a bare `&&` with
# nothing else in between, the checkout runs if-and-only-if that `cd`
# succeeded -- base_dir is provably NOT where it executes, so keeping it as a
# candidate here is a false positive on `cd <linked-worktree> && git checkout
# ...`, not extra scrutiny (the doc's own linked-worktree exemption).
# Any other join keeps the fail-closed default: `;` (or `|`, or an
# intervening command, or no `cd` at all) lets the `cd` fail silently while
# the checkout still runs in base_dir, so base_dir must stay a candidate.
if [ -n "$cd_targets" ]; then
  last_cd=$(printf '%s' "$cd_scope" \
    | grep -boE '(^|[;&|(])[[:space:]]*cd[[:space:]]+[^[:space:];&|]+' | tail -n1 || true)
  if [ -n "$last_cd" ]; then
    last_cd_off=${last_cd%%:*}
    last_cd_text=${last_cd#*:}
    last_cd_bytes=$(printf '%s' "$last_cd_text" | wc -c)
    gap=$(printf '%s' "$cd_scope" | tail -c "+$((last_cd_off + last_cd_bytes + 1))")
    grep -Eq '^[[:space:]]*&&[[:space:]]*$' <<<"$gap" && dirs=""
  fi
  while IFS= read -r ct; do
    [ -z "$ct" ] && continue
    case "$ct" in /*) dirs="$dirs
$ct" ;; *) dirs="$dirs
$base_dir/$ct" ;; esac
  done <<<"$cd_targets"
fi

# `-C <path>` inside the isolated `git … checkout|switch` statement itself.
c_target=$(printf '%s' "$seg" | grep -Eo -- '-C[[:space:]]+[^[:space:]]+' | sed -n '1p' \
  | sed -E 's/^-C[[:space:]]+//' || true)
if [ -n "$c_target" ]; then
  case "$c_target" in /*) dirs="$dirs
$c_target" ;; *) dirs="$dirs
$base_dir/$c_target" ;; esac
fi

# --- repo gate + root-checkout-vs-worktree, unioned over every candidate ----
# In scope, and a real target of this switch, the moment ANY candidate is
# BOTH an inc-b2c-mvp checkout AND the ROOT checkout (not a linked worktree).
is_target_root=0
dir=""
while IFS= read -r d; do
  [ -z "$d" ] && continue
  [ -d "$d" ] || continue
  remote=$(git -C "$d" remote get-url origin 2>/dev/null || true)
  case "$remote" in *inc-b2c-mvp*) ;; *) continue ;; esac
  gitdir=$(git -C "$d" rev-parse --absolute-git-dir 2>/dev/null || true)
  common=$(git -C "$d" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir 2>/dev/null || true)
  # Older git lacks --path-format; fall back and absolutise by hand.
  if [ -z "$common" ]; then
    common=$(git -C "$d" rev-parse --git-common-dir 2>/dev/null || true)
    [ -n "$common" ] && case "$common" in /*) ;; *) common="$(cd -P "$d" && pwd)/$common" ;; esac
  fi
  [ -n "$gitdir" ] && [ -n "$common" ] || continue
  gitdir=$(cd -P "$gitdir" 2>/dev/null && pwd) || continue
  common=$(cd -P "$common" 2>/dev/null && pwd) || continue
  # Match -> root checkout (not a linked worktree, where branch work belongs).
  if [ "$gitdir" = "$common" ]; then
    is_target_root=1
    dir="$d"
    break
  fi
done <<<"$dirs"
[ "$is_target_root" -eq 1 ] || exit 0

# --- is this a branch switch, or a pathspec restore? -----------------------
# A `--` separator means everything after it is a pathspec: HEAD does not move.
grep -Eq -- '(^|[[:space:]])--([[:space:]]|$)' <<<"$seg" && exit 0

# Strip the head (`git [-C dir] [flags] checkout|switch`) and inspect the rest.
rest=${seg#*checkout}
case "$seg" in *switch*) [ "$rest" = "$seg" ] && rest=${seg#*switch} ;; esac

creates=""
grep -Eq -- '(^|[[:space:]])(-b|-B|-c|-C|--orphan)([[:space:]]|$)' <<<"$rest" && creates=1

# First non-flag token = the target ref (or a pathspec).
target=""
for tok in $rest; do
  case "$tok" in -*) continue ;; esac
  target="$tok"
  break
done

# `git checkout main` / `git switch main`: the documented remediation.
if [ -z "$creates" ] && { [ "$target" = "main" ] || [ "$target" = "origin/main" ]; }; then
  exit 0
fi

# Pathspec restore without `--`: `git checkout package.json`, `git checkout .`
# The token names something that exists on disk, so it is a file, not a branch.
if [ -z "$creates" ] && [ -n "$target" ] && [ -e "$dir/$target" ]; then
  exit 0
fi

# Nothing to switch to and nothing created -> `git checkout` bare / flags only.
[ -z "$creates" ] && [ -z "$target" ] && exit 0

jq -n --arg r "Blocked: this switches the ROOT checkout off main. Many agents run in parallel from the shared root checkout and spawn worktrees off it, switching its branch puts every other agent on the wrong base, and uncommitted edits there contaminate their docker-test/docker-eval builds. Do branch work in a worktree instead: git worktree add -b <branch> ../wt-<slug> origin/main (see .agents/skills/plan-build-isolated/SKILL.md Phase 0). 'git checkout main' stays allowed; INC_ALLOW_ROOT_CHECKOUT=1 disables this guard." \
  '{hookSpecificOutput:{hookEventName:"PreToolUse",permissionDecision:"deny",permissionDecisionReason:$r}}'
exit 0
